sections.title: The Collection Journey Through Macedonia and Asia

blocks.text: Acts 20 opens with Paul's departure from Ephesus following an uproar, his travel through Macedonia exhorting churches, and a three-month stay in Greece. A plot against Paul as he prepares to sail for Syria redirects him back through Macedonia instead of the coastal route. The return journey includes a multi-city delegation: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, Tychicus, and Trophimus from Asia. Acts explicitly preserves this diversity of origins without claiming a unified institutional status or formal purpose for the traveling party.
